rules.sentence: Dilated cardiomyopathy vs. left-dominant arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
Dilated cardiomyopathy vs. left-dominant arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
ECG abnormalities	Left ventricular hypertrophy with a strain pattern of ST-segment; left bundle branch block
ECG abnormalities	Low QRS voltages in limb leads; negative T waves in lateral leads; negative T waves in right precordial leads (biventricular form)
Echocardiography and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging findings	Dilated and hypokinetic LV with no or patchy non-ischaemic (mid-myocardial) LGE (septum)
Echocardiography and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging findings	Non-dilated and hypokinetic LV with large amount of non-ischemic (subepicardial) LGE (inferolateral LV wall)
Systolic LV dysfunction unrelated to the global extent of LGE
Systolic LV dysfunction related to the global extent of LGE
Types of ventricular arrhythmias	PVBs and NSVT (RBBB pattern); sustained VT(uncommon); VF
Types of ventricular arrhythmias	PVBs, NSVT, and monomorphic sustained VT (RBBB pattern; both LBBB and RBBB patterns in biventricular form); VF
Mechanism of VT	Scar-related or functional re-entry (branch to branch re-entry)
Most common site of VT origin	Intramural septum
Most common site of VT origin	Subepicardial infero-lateral LV free wall
